Question Choices: Fill: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One exterior angle measures $72^\circ$. What is the measure of the corresponding interior angle in degrees?
Hints: Corresponding angles are in the exact same position at each intersection
Solution: Corresponding angles occupy the same position at the two intersections. Since the lines are parallel they are equal, so the other angle is 72°.

Question Choices: Fill: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one interior angle is $105^\circ$, what is the measure of the alternate interior angle in degrees?
Solution: Alternate interior angles on opposite sides of the transversal are equal when the lines are parallel. Therefore the other angle is 105°.

Question Choices: Fill: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle formed is $54^\circ$. Find the measure of its supplementary angle in degrees.
Hints: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees
Solution: The requested pair is supplementary, so x+54=180°. Thus x=126°.

Question Choices: Fill: Two angles $(5x + 8)^\circ$ and $(3x + 30)^\circ$ form a pair of vertical angles. Find $x$.
Solution: Vertical angles are equal: (5 × x + 8)=(3 × x + 30). Collect variable terms and solve to get x=11. Substitution gives 63° in BOTH expressions, so the equality checks.

Question Choices: Fill: An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles of $35^\circ$. Find the vertex angle in degrees.
Hints: The three angles must add up to 180 degrees
Solution: Two equal base angles each measure 35°. Vertex angle=180−2(35)=110°. Check: 35+35+110=180°.
